summary.value: The Old English Pheasant Fowl is a light utility chicken from the farms of northern England, chiefly Yorkshire and Lancashire, with roots in Cumberland and Westmorland too. It is a very old breed, known earlier as the Yorkshire Pheasant, Golden Pheasant or Old-fashioned Pheasant, and it got its present name and a breed club around 1914. Some think it helped give rise to the Hamburg. Its mahogany feathers edged with darker lacing recall a wild pheasant. It has a rose comb and white earlobes. Roosters weigh about 6 to 7 pounds and hens about 5 to 6 pounds. Hens lay white eggs, around 160 a year, and the birds carry a meaty breast for a light breed. They are hardy and thrive on free range, which made them a farm favorite. Today the breed is rare.
